_about: The extra MCP servers a PA may switch on from its chat (design: TheCrew/design/Round 4 - PA tools and MCP switching.md, sections 1-2; Kris confirmed the risk classes 2026-10-27). Kris edits THIS file; crew/mcp_catalog.py turns it into OpenCode mcp entries and decides what a PA may do. One entry per server in Crush's mcp block (%LOCALAPPDATA%/crush/crush.json), except crew itself, which every PA always has. `from` is the server's name in crush.json; `class` is the risk class below; `_why` says, in one line, why it is in that class. The catalogue IS the policy: changing what a PA may switch on means editing a class rule or a server's class here, never code.

classes._about: What a PA may do with a server of each class. `on` is the rule for switching a server ON: allow = no question; ask_once = Kris approves the first time in a chat, then it may be switched freely until the chat ends; ask = Kris's approval every time; deny = never. crew/mcp_catalog.decide() reads these rules; server.py (crew_mcp) asks it and obeys.

read._why: Read-only tools (a document, a paper, a package's docs): nothing on this machine or on any account changes, so switching it on costs nothing to undo.

local_act._why: Drives something real on THIS machine (the Godot editor, a browser, the vault): one wrong call changes live state, so Kris approves the first switch in a chat and not every one after.

account._why: Acts as Kris on an account OUTSIDE this machine (GitHub, Sentry, Penpot): a mistake leaves this machine, so every switch needs Kris, not once per chat.

never._why: Kris never wants a PA to reach it: no gate, nothing the crew can check, so the catalogue refuses it outright.
